title: Scrolling over volume slider in popup does not keep OSD in sync with it as the volume changes
line: After scrolling over a volume slider in the Audio Volume popup, the slider again follows volume changes made with the tray icon wheel, volume keys or other apps.
explanation: The popup's volume slider gets its position from a binding to the device volume. Scrolling over it (or pressing arrow keys on it) assigned the value directly, which removed that binding; only releasing a drag restored it. From then on, volume changes made elsewhere (tray icon wheel, volume keys, other apps) showed in the OSD but not in the popup slider or its percentage, even after reopening the popup. Peder Bergan's open MR plasma-pa!440 replaces the plain binding with an explicit Binding element that is only paused while the handle is dragged, so it survives the wheel and key assignments; stepped values are rounded to whole device units.

commits.message:
applet: Restore volume slider synchronization after wheel changes

Wheel and keyboard step changes assign value, removing its binding to the
device volume. Only a mouse release reinstalls it, leaving subsequent
external volume changes invisible in the popup.

Use an explicit Binding that keeps monitoring volume after assignments and
is disabled while dragging. Reapply it on release without restoring the
old value when the drag begins.

BUG: 527034

media.caption: Pure master: two wheel notches over the popup slider (50% to 35%), then four over the tray icon (OSD 55%) and two volume-down keys (45%); the popup slider stays at 35%.
With plasma-pa!440: same steps; the popup slider follows to 55% and then 45%.
Pure master, after scrolling over the tray icon: OSD says 55%, popup slider still 35%.
With the fix, same moment: popup slider at 55%.
Pure master, after two volume-down keys: real volume 45% (tooltip), popup slider still 35%.
With the fix, same moment: popup slider at 45%.

review.text: Clean, idiomatic fix from open MR plasma-pa!440 replacing the fragile inline binding and manual Qt.binding() restore in ListItemBase.qml with an explicit Binding on value paused only while slider.pressed is true (with Binding.RestoreNone), plus rounding stepped volume deltas. It preserves drag behavior and PulseAudio rejection sync while keeping the slider synchronized after wheel and keyboard changes, clearly demonstrated by the before/after evidence.

reviews.text: Clean, idiomatic fix from open MR plasma-pa!440 replacing the fragile inline binding and manual Qt.binding() restore in ListItemBase.qml with an explicit Binding on value paused only while slider.pressed is true (with Binding.RestoreNone), plus rounding stepped volume deltas. It preserves drag behavior and PulseAudio rejection sync while keeping the slider synchronized after wheel and keyboard changes, clearly demonstrated by the before/after evidence.

Correct cause: the wheel/key path assigned slider.value, destroying its binding to the device volume, and only a drag release restored it. A Binding on value (when: !pressed, RestoreNone) survives those imperative assignments and still re-syncs on release, which also covers the old 'PA rejected the change' case the removed comment handled; rounding to whole volume units is harmless. Media show the popup slider following tray-wheel and volume-key changes after the fix and stuck before. Minor nit only: with the binding live during wheel steps, an out-of-order PA echo during very fast scrolling could briefly snap the slider back a step, but that is unlikely at local PA latency and not a blocker.
